ety.text: 16th century Middle French athéisme, from athée (“atheist”), a loan from Ancient Greek ἄθεος (átheos, “godless”, from ἀ- (a-, “without”) + θεός (theós, “deity, god”)). First English attestation dates to 1587 (OED).

senses.d: Belief that no deities exist (sometimes including rejection of other religious beliefs).
A lack of belief in deities, or a belief that there is insufficient evidence to believe in a god.
Absence of belief that any deities exist (including absence of the concept of deities).
ex: What can parents do, and mothers more especially, […] with regard to the atheism that is natural to all the children of men?

senses.d: Neglect of one's obligations to God; behavior incongruent with belief in God (regardless of belief in the strict sense).
Absence of belief in a particular deity, pantheon, or religious doctrine (notwithstanding belief in other deities).
A rejection of all religions, even non-theistic ones.
ex: Another reason why the transition between Buddhism and atheism seemed so easy, was my personal discomfort with the theory of reincarnation.

grp.label: belief that no deities exist (sometimes including rejection of other religious beliefs)
lack of belief that any deities exist (with or without a belief that no deities exist)

ety.text: From ateu + -ismo or French athéisme.

chain.g: an atheist; one who rejected the gods worshipped by the wider society.

senses.d: A person who does not believe in deities or gods.
A person who is certain that no deities exist or who thinks that the existence of deities can be disproven.
ex: Ageine, the Atheistes, which say in their hartes there is no God; […]

senses.d: A person who doubts the existence of deities (therefore, an agnostic may be considered an atheist).
Any person lacking belief in deities (including children who are unaware of religion).
ex: All children are born Atheists; they have no idea of God. Are they then criminal on account of their ignorance?

senses.d: A person who does not believe in a particular deity (but may believe in another deity).
A person who does not believe in any religion (not even a religion without gods); a nonreligious person.
Of or relating to atheists or atheism; atheistic.
ex: He would have been seven times more Epicure and atheist than he was.

senses.d: To make someone an atheist.

grp.label: a person who believes with certainty that no deities exist
a person who doubts the existence of deities — see also agnostic

chain.g: an atheist; one who rejected the gods worshipped by the wider society.

From Middle English athlete, from Latin āthlēta (and probably also partly from Middle French athlete), from Ancient Greek ἀθλητής (athlētḗs), from ἀθλέω (athléō, “compete for a prize”), from ἆθλον (âthlon, “prize”) or ἆθλος (âthlos, “competition”).

senses.d: A participant in any of a group of sporting activities including track and field, road running, cross country running and racewalking.
A person who actively participates in physical sports, especially with great skill; a sportsperson.
ex: She's the first athlete in her sport to obtain a corporate sponsor.

senses.d: An exceptionally physically fit person.

grp.label: participant in track and field, road running, cross country running, or racewalking
person who actively participates in physical sports
